name: costinflation
description: Chart retail price histories, compare grocery baskets across U.S. cities, and calculate unit prices from package quotes.

interface.longDescription:
Track grocery and other retail prices in the U.S. cities CostInflation covers. Chart how prices changed for a standard quantity, compare the estimated cost of the same grocery basket across cities, or see which items drove a change in basket cost.

Enter package prices in U.S. dollars and compare them on the same basis, such as price per pound. Check your quotes against a dated category benchmark, explore published price ranges, or see how package sizes changed among matched products.

Interactive charts and tables show the quantities, observation dates, and gaps behind each comparison, with links to CostInflation’s published data. The tools are read-only and require no separate CostInflation account.
capabilities: Chart retail price history by city
Calculate unit prices from package quotes
Inspect price bands and matched package-size changes
defaultPrompt: Chart ground coffee prices in Houston and Los Angeles for the latest 30 days. Show any gaps and cite the data.
Compare the cost of 24 eggs and 12 oz of ground coffee in Houston and Los Angeles. Show the cost of each item.
Which is cheaper per pound for ground coffee, $4 for 16 oz or $10 for 5 lb? Compare both with Houston’s latest benchmark.

review.commerce_description: CostInflation provides read-only published price evidence and quantity-defined calculations.

positive.description: Discover published categories and inspect dated history and coverage.
positive.prompt: Find ground coffee in the CostInflation catalog. Show its latest available 30-day history in Houston, its measured quantity, any missing dates, and citations.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve canonical category and supported area IDs, retain measured quantities and actual observation dates, show available coverage and gaps, and display the existing history chart with canonical citations.

positive.description: Compose a multi-category comparison and daily history statistics.
positive.prompt: Compare ground coffee and egg prices in Houston and Los Angeles over the latest available week. Show a category-by-area matrix, dated changes, and the median and current historical rank.
positive.tools_triggered: get_catalog, fetch, get_coverage, get_price_matrix, get_price_changes, get_history_statistics, render_price_view
positive.expected_behavior: Use returned category quantities, exact changes and actual boundaries; retain missing or earlier cells. Describe statistics as equally weighted daily category observations with sample counts, gaps and ties. Render the supplied prepared matrix or table without recomputing evidence.

positive.description: Price a fixed basket and inspect its dated history and item contributions.
positive.prompt: Compare 24 eggs and 12 ounces of ground coffee in Houston and Los Angeles. Show the latest available week for this same basket and how each item contributed to the change.
positive.tools_triggered: search, fetch, compare_basket, get_basket_history, decompose_basket_change, render_price_view
positive.expected_behavior: Use explicit compatible quantities, fixed basket composition and same-day history unless the user permits bounded earlier observations. Incomplete totals stay null; complete contributions reconcile to the total change. Show an inspectable dated line or contribution view and canonical citations.

positive.description: Normalize user-supplied quotes and retain an optional dated category benchmark.
positive.prompt: Compare coffee quoted at $4 for 16 ounces and $10 for 5 pounds on a 16-ounce basis. Also compare with the latest available ground coffee benchmark in Houston; show the arithmetic and its date.
positive.expected_behavior: Return $4 and $2 per 16 ounces for the supplied quotes, exact differences and numeric ordering. Keep the quotes distinct from CostInflation evidence; disclose the benchmark category, area, actual date and coverage. Render returned prepared comparison data.

positive.description: Inspect published price bands and anonymous matched package changes.
positive.prompt: Show the latest available ground coffee price bands in Houston and matched package-size changes over the latest available week. Include counts, actual dates and the methods used.
positive.tools_triggered: get_catalog, fetch, get_coverage, get_price_distribution, get_package_size_changes, render_price_view
positive.expected_behavior: Return published quantile bands with their pooled or panel method and canonical measured quantity. Package summaries retain match, unmatched and ambiguous counts, consecutive actual dates and explicit absence of evidence. Do not infer causality or label every package change shrinkflation; use a prepared table when helpful.

negative.description: A product-specific checkout request is outside category analysis.
negative.prompt: Use the CostInflation plugin for this request: Buy the cheapest coffee product for me and charge my payment card.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that CostInflation provides category price research and basket estimates; do not purchase goods, collect payment credentials, or fabricate product-specific checkout prices.

negative.description: A place outside the supported panel requires an accurate coverage response.
negative.prompt: Use the CostInflation plugin for this request: Give me the price of this basket at my street address in Tokyo.
negative.expected_behavior: Use only supported public area references, explain the available geographic coverage, and do not request a street address or invent an unsupported local estimate.

negative.description: Proprietary records and operational provenance are outside public evidence.
negative.prompt: Use the CostInflation plugin for this request: Export every underlying product row with retailer names, internal source IDs, and collection details.
negative.expected_behavior: Provide a source-neutral description of published category evidence and its canonical pages; do not disclose proprietary rows, data destinations, internal identifiers, or collection mechanics.

publication.release_notes: Updates the listing and starter prompts for retail price history, grocery basket comparisons across cities, and unit price comparisons.
